newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-START OF INDY 500 MARRED BY FORMATION LAP WRECK.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-START OF INDY 500 MARRED BY FORMATION LAP WRECK.

text.p: The start of the rain-postponed Indianapolis 500 was delayed briefly on Monday when a crash during the formation lap wiped out the entire fifth row of the 35-car field.

The cars of Brazilian Affonso Giaffone, Swede Kenny Brack and Frenchman Stephan Gregoire -- all of which were to start from the fifth row -- ended up smashed into the wall at the entrance to turn four as the field was getting set to take the green flag.

The start of 81st Indianapolis 500 was held up while the track was cleared of debris and the damaged cars removed. The three disappointed drivers were not immediately sure what had happened and said they would have to review video tape before placing any blame for the incident.

Several other drivers were also experiencing mechanical difficulties before the start or early in the race, which was postponed from Sunday after rain drenched the world's most famous oval race track, known as the old brickyard.
The race did get underway, but more rain brought out the red flag and the event was halted after 16 laps of the 200-lap classic.
More than $8 million in prizes are expected to be posted for the event, with the winner being assured of a purse in excess of $1 million.
